CAN THIS ENVIRONMENT SEARCH THE INTERNET ARCHIVE'S FULL TEXT? NO, AND HERE IS
THE CONTROL THAT PROVES IT.
Tested 2026-09-07 under p_463, whose first step was exactly this question.

=====================================================================
THE THREE ROUTES, ALL TESTED
=====================================================================

1. advancedsearch.php -- METADATA ONLY. Already established: it rejects the
   full-text parameter outright, returning UNSUPPORTED_VALUE for sin=TXT
   (f_5260). Every enumeration this project has run is a catalogue search.

2. THE ARCHIVE'S OWN FULL-TEXT APIS -- UNREACHABLE FROM HERE.
     https://ia-pub-fts-api.archive.org/search/v1/scrape?q=...   HTTP 000
     https://ia-fts.archive.org/api/v1/search/hits?q=...          HTTP 000
   Both drop the tunnel, the same failure the proxy logs as
   ws_closed_mid_exchange. They are separate hosts from archive.org, which has
   been reachable all day for metadata and multi-megabyte downloads -- the
   per-host pattern of rule 45 again.

3. OPEN LIBRARY'S search/inside -- REACHABLE, AND BOOKS-ONLY.
   This is the route p_463 called "the one route to IA full text that works
   from here", and it does work. It is also the wrong index for this question.

=====================================================================
THE CONTROL, WHICH IS THE POINT
=====================================================================

A quoted "Kanawana" search of search/inside returns SEVENTY-SIX ITEMS. Every
one is a published book, periodical or directory: almanacs, guides to summer
camps, Handbook of South American Indians, two Japanese-English dictionaries,
the McGraw-Hill directory, the Sessional Papers.

NOT ONE ITEM FROM THE YMCA OF MONTREAL FONDS OR THE CONCORDIA COLLECTIONS
APPEARS. No Georgian, no Green Triangle, no News Bulletin, no annual report.

AND THIS IS NOT AN ARGUMENT FROM ABSENCE, BECAUSE THE CONTROL IS IN HAND.
Earlier the same day, under p_462, forty-six of those fonds items were
downloaded in full and grepped. FOUR OF THEM CONTAIN THE WORD:

    the-news-bulletin-vol-15-no-01              Kanawana x1
    sgw-ymca-annual-report-1959-short-version   Kanawana x3
    national-council-bulletin-vol-36-no-04      Kanawana x1
    bulletin-1970-02-13                         Kanawana x1

All four are full-text items on the Internet Archive. All four contain the
exact string. NONE OF THE FOUR IS IN THE SEVENTY-SIX. The index does not reach
them.

=====================================================================
WHAT THAT SETTLES
=====================================================================

p_463's question was whether the seventy-six-item ceiling is the corpus's or
the instrument's. IT IS THE INSTRUMENT'S, and precisely: search/inside indexes
BOOKS, and the archive's non-book scanned texts -- exactly the class the
Concordia and YMCA collections belong to -- are outside it.

SO THE GEORGIAN QUESTION CANNOT BE ANSWERED FROM HERE. Three hundred and
forty-one issues of Sir George Williams' student newspaper sit in
rma-concordia-publications; sgw-concordia-connection.md has asked since
2026-07-09 whether any of them covered the camp; and no name search will ever
surface them, because a student newspaper is catalogued by date and its
contents are not in the book index.

TWO WAYS FORWARD, AND BOTH ARE REAL:
  * A PERSON WITH A BROWSER at archive.org's own full-text search, which is
    where the ia-fts APIs above serve the website. One query, all collections.
  * OR BRUTE FORCE FROM HERE, which is now known to work: the p_462 sweep
    downloaded forty-six items in full and searched them in about four
    minutes. Three hundred and forty-one Georgian issues is a larger job of
    the same shape, not a different one. THE FILENAME TRAP APPLIES -- the
    djvu.txt is named after the item's TITLE, not its identifier -- and the
    metadata call gives the right name.

The second option is the honest recommendation. The instrument this project
lacks is not access; it is an index. It can build its own by downloading.
